blocks.en: G.9 Evaluation on Math500
blocks.zh: G.9 对数学500的评价

blocks.en: We additionally evaluate mathematical reasoning on Math500 [ 101 ] . This setting is intentionally challenging for our training distribution: the student is distilled from GPT-5-Chat on LMSYS-Chat, where only 3.4 % 3.4\% of the training prompts are math-related. Thus, Math500 measures whether black-box distillation preserves and transfers sparse reasoning ability from a mostly general conversational dataset, rather than whether the method is specialized for math training.
blocks.zh: 我们额外评价了数学推理在Math500 [101]. 这种环境对我们的训练分配有意具有挑战性:学生从LMSYS-Chat上的GPT-5-Chat中提炼出来,其中只有3.4%的训练提示与数学有关。 因此,Math500衡量黑盒蒸馏是否保存并转移了大部分是一般对话数据集的稀疏推理能力,而不是该方法是否专门用于数学培训.

blocks.en: We compute Math500 accuracy with a rule-based answer-matching protocol rather than an LLM judge. Each model is prompted with the standard instruction wrapper plus an explicit request to put the final answer in \boxed{} , and responses are generated greedily. For each output, we extract the final answer by first taking the last \boxed{} expression, then falling back to answers after #### , explicit phrases such as “final answer is”, and finally the last mathematical expression or number. The extracted answer is compared against the dataset’s final_answer field using exact string match after LaTeX normalization, numerical comparison with tolerance 10 − 6 10^{-6} for numbers and fractions, and SymPy-based symbolic equivalence when available. Extraction failures are counted as incorrect, and accuracy is the percentage of correct examples among the 500 Math500 problems.
blocks.zh: 我们用一个基于规则的答案匹配程序而不是LLM法官来计算Math500的准确性. 每个模型都通过标准指令包装器 加上明确要求将最后的答案放入\boxed QQ)中, 反应被贪婪地产生. 对于每个输出,我们先提取最后的答案,先取最后一个\boxedQQ表达式,然后回到QQ之后的答案,像“最后答案是”这样的明确短语,最后取最后一个数学表达式或数字. LaTeX 正常化后使用精确的字符串匹配、数字和分数与容性10 - 6 10 - 6 6 的数值比较, 采掘失败被算作不正确,准确性是500 Math500问题中正确例子的百分比.

blocks.en: Table 19 shows that naive sequence-level imitation can hurt mathematical reasoning: SeqKD drops from the undistilled model’s 46.4 % 46.4\% accuracy to 39.8 % 39.8\% . GAD partially recovers this degradation, reaching 44.0 % 44.0\% , but still remains below the original student. In contrast, GRGC achieves 49.6 % 49.6\% , outperforming the undistilled model and both distillation baselines. This result is consistent with our main claim: by improving grouped advantage construction from adversarial rewards, GRGC provides a better-conditioned on-policy signal that can exploit the limited math-related supervision in LMSYS-Chat without degrading the student’s reasoning ability.
blocks.zh: 表19显示天真序列级仿真会伤害数学推理: SeqKD从未固定模型的46.4%46.4%的精度下降到39.8%39.8 %。 GAD部分恢复了这种退化,达到44.0%的44.0%,但仍低于原来的学生. 与此相反,GRGC实现了49.6%的49.6\%,优于未蒸馏模型和两种蒸馏基线。 这个结果符合我们的主要主张:GRGC通过对抗性奖励来改进组合优势构建,提供了一个条件更好的政策信号,可以利用LMSYS-Chat中有限的数学相关监管,而不贬低学生的推理能力.

blocks.en: G.10 Multi-seed Evaluation Robustness
blocks.zh: G.10 多种子评价

blocks.en:
The automatic evaluation results in the main paper use the default evaluation seed, i.e. , Seed=0.
To verify that the observed gains do not come from judge-sampling randomness, we additionally repeat the Qwen2.5-72B automatic evaluation with five evaluation seeds while keeping the model generations fixed.
Tables 20 and 21 report both the individual seed results and the mean/std across seeds.
The results are robust across evaluation seeds: the standard deviation is only 0.03 0.03 for our normalized score and 0.53 0.53 for win rate, while the improvement of GRGC over GAD is much larger than these fluctuations.
This confirms that the performance gains of GRGC are robust to evaluation-seed variation rather than being an artifact of a particular judge sample.
blocks.zh:

表20和表21分别报告了各个种子的结果和种子的平均值。
各种评价种子的结果都非常有力:我们正常得分的标准差只有0.03 0.03,胜率只有0.53 0.53,而GRGC比GAD的改进远大于这些波动。

The key practical implication is that GRGC does not introduce an extra rollout loop, an extra critic network, or another model-scale optimization stage; its additional cost comes only from cheap per-group operations after the main neural computation has already been done.
In particular, BT loss formation, GRPO normalization, OT matching, and group power shaping are all low-order operations on scalar group rewards after the dominant neural computation is finished. Since N N is small and fixed in our setting, these terms do not materially affect end-to-end training time, so the overall wall-clock training cost of GRGC is expected to be nearly the same as that of GAD.

blocks.en: Appendix I Broader Impact
blocks.zh: 附录一 更广泛的影响

blocks.en: Our work studies how to make black-box distillation more effective when the teacher is accessible only through output queries. On the positive side, better black-box distillation can reduce the cost of obtaining capable small language models, which may improve accessibility for research labs, educational use, and resource-constrained deployment settings. It may also enable more systematic study of proprietary-model behavior using open students that are easier to inspect, evaluate, and stress-test.
blocks.zh: 我们的工作研究了如何在老师只能通过输出查询获得时,使黑盒蒸馏效果更好. 积极的一面是,更好的黑箱蒸馏可以降低获得有能力的小型语言模型的成本,这可以改善研究实验室的无障碍性,教育用途,以及资源约束的部署设置. 还可以利用开放型学生更系统地研究专有型行为,这些学生更容易检查、评价和压力测试。

blocks.en: At the same time, improvements in distillation efficiency can also accelerate the transfer of undesirable behaviors from proprietary teachers into cheaper and more deployable students. More capable distilled models may be misused for low-cost spam generation, manipulative persuasion, or unsafe domain advice. In addition, more effective distillation can make capability transfer easier to reproduce, which is a dual-use concern. Our method does not require additional access to private model internals or private data, but it can increase the effectiveness of capability transfer from black-box teachers. We therefore view stronger safety evaluation, misuse screening, and downstream deployment constraints as important complements to progress in black-box distillation.
blocks.zh: 同时,蒸馏效率的提高也可以加速将不良行为从专有教师转移到更便宜且更可部署的学生身上. 更有能力的蒸馏模型可能被滥用于低成本的垃圾邮件生成、操纵说服或不安全域咨询。 此外,更有效的蒸馏可使能力转让更容易复制,这是双重用途问题。 我们的方法不需要额外访问私人模型内部或私人数据,但可以提高黑盒教师的能力转移的有效性. 因此,我们认为,加强安全评估、滥用筛选和下游部署限制是黑箱蒸馏进展的重要补充。

blocks.en: Appendix J Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录J 限制

blocks.en: Our method is built on top of GAD and inherits both its strengths and its limitations. In particular, although GRGC improves the quality of on-policy black-box distillation, it still relies on an adversarial critic and on-policy rollouts, and is therefore typically slower than simple supervised baselines such as SeqKD. This is a real tradeoff: our goal is not to make on-policy distillation cheaper than off-policy imitation in absolute terms, but to make the extra optimization cost buy a better-conditioned and more effective training signal.
blocks.zh: 我们的方法建立在性别与发展的基础上,并继承其优势和局限性。 特别是,GRGC虽然提高了政策上黑箱蒸馏的质量,但仍然依赖于对抗性的批评者和政策上推出,因此通常比SeqKD等简单的监督基准慢. 这是一个真正的权衡:我们的目标不是使政策上的提炼在绝对值上比政策外的模仿便宜,而是使额外的优化成本买入一个条件更好和更有效的培训信号。

blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and introduction state the core claim that GRGC improves on-policy black-box distillation by conditioning prompt-group reward geometry, and this matches the method, experiments, and limitations discussed in the paper; see the abstract, Section 1, and Section 5. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper includes an explicit Limitations discussion in the appendix, covering the additional training cost relative to SeqKD; see Appendix “Limitations”. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The appendix provides explicit assumptions, formal propositions, and corresponding derivations and proof sketches for the theoretical claims used in the paper; see Appendix “Mechanism Analysis for OT Calibration and Group Power”. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper specifies datasets, model families, teacher models, evaluation benchmarks, key hyperparameters, training schedule, and hardware used for the reported experiments; see Section 4.1 and the appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper and appendix provide the datasets, model families, evaluation prompts, pseudocode, hyperparameters, and reproduction-relevant implementation details needed to reproduce the main experiments. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 4.1 and the appendix describe datasets, evaluation splits, teacher and student models, baselines, training schedule, group size, learning rates, OT and power hyperparameters, sensitivity analyses for the two method-specific hyperparameters, and hardware. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper reports multi-seed automatic evaluation results with mean and standard deviation across five evaluation seeds in the Appendix, showing that the gains remain much larger than judge-sampling variability. It also supports the empirical conclusions through consistent trends across multiple teacher-student pairs, multiple test sets, sensitivity analyses, training-stability analyses, and complementary human evaluation. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper specifies the accelerator type and count, the training schedule in epochs and optimization steps, the key sequence lengths, and the overall training recipe used for the reported experiments; see Section 4.1 and Appendix “Complexity Analysis”. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: To the best of our knowledge, the research conforms to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics; the paper also discusses broader impacts and limitations, including dual-use concerns. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper discusses both positive impacts (cheaper, more accessible small models) and negative impacts (more effective transfer of harmful behaviors), and also mentions the need for safeguards; see the main-paper Broader Impact paragraph and the appendix Broader Impact section. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This submission does not release a new high-risk model, model checkpoint, or scraped dataset asset; the paper instead discusses broader-impact risks and deployment considerations. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The paper credits the datasets, models, and baseline methods used in the experiments and identifies the main external assets explicitly in the experimental sections and references. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The current submission does not release a new dataset, benchmark, model checkpoint, or public code package as an asset. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The appendix describes the human-evaluation setup, the annotator pool, the per-model sample allocation, and the evaluation criteria used by the annotators. The study does not rely on an external crowdsourcing platform. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The human evaluation concerns expert assessment of model outputs only, does not involve collection of personal or sensitive participant data, and is described in the appendix together with the evaluation procedure and scope of human involvement. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: The core contribution is a reward-geometry conditioning method for black-box distillation rather than a method that uses an LLM as a novel algorithmic component; teacher and judge models are standard experimental ingredients and are documented in Section 4.1. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 抽象和引言陈述了核心说法,即GRGC通过调制即时群奖励几何来改进政策上的黑盒蒸馏,这与论文中讨论的方法,实验和限制相匹配;见抽象,第一节和第五节. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 该文件在附录中明确讨论了限制问题,涉及与SeqKD有关的额外培训费用;见附录“限制”。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 附录为文件中所用的理论索赔提供了明确的假设、正式命题以及相应的推论和证明草图;见附录“OT校准和群力的机械分析”。 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 文件具体规定了数据集、模范家庭、教师模型、评价基准、关键超参数、培训时间表和用于所报告实验的硬件;见第4.1节和附录。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 论文和附录提供了复制主要实验所需的数据集、模型家族、评价提示、伪码、超参数以及复制相关实施细节。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 回答:[是] 说明:第4.1节和附录描述了数据集、评价划分、师生模型、基线、培训时间表、小组规模、学习率、OT和功率超参数、两种方法特有的超参数的敏感性分析以及硬件。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 该文件报告了附录中五个评价种子的多种子自动评价结果,其平均值和标准偏差表明,收益仍然比判断抽样的可变性大得多。 它还通过多个师生对对、多个测试组、敏感性分析、培训稳定性分析以及补充人的评价,支持经验性结论。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 论文规定了加速器类型和计数、时代和优化步骤的训练时间表、关键序列长度以及报告实验所用的总体训练方法;见第4.1节和附录“复杂性分析”。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 据我们所知,这项研究符合《新IPS道德守则》;该文件还讨论了更广泛的影响和限制,包括双重用途问题。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 文件既讨论了积极影响(便宜、更易获取的小模型),也讨论了负面影响(有害行为的更有效转移),并提到需要保障措施;见主要文件 " 广义影响 " 段落和附录 " 广义影响 " 一节。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文件没有发布新的高风险模式、检查站模式或报废数据集资产,而是讨论了影响更广的风险和部署方面的考虑。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 该文件对实验中使用的数据集、模型和基准方法给予肯定,并在实验章节和参考文献中明确确定了主要的外部资产。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[不详]理由: 当前提交的数据不作为资产发布新的数据集,基准,模式检查站,或公共代码包. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 附录描述了人评价设置,注释员池,按型号进行抽样分配,以及注释员所用的评价标准. 研究不依靠外部的众包平台. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 人类评价只涉及对模型产出的专家评估,不涉及收集个人或敏感的参与者数据,附录中结合评价程序和人类参与的范围加以说明。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[不详]理由: 核心贡献是黑箱蒸馏的奖励-几何调节方法,而不是使用LLM作为新算法组件的方法;教师和判断模型是标准实验成分,并在第4.1节中记录. · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Claims
blocks.zh: 索偿

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The abstract and introduction state the core claim that GRGC improves on-policy black-box distillation by conditioning prompt-group reward geometry, and this matches the method, experiments, and limitations discussed in the paper; see the abstract, Section 1, and Section 5.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 抽象和引言陈述了核心说法,即GRGC通过调制即时群奖励几何来改进政策上的黑盒蒸馏,这与论文中讨论的方法,实验和限制相匹配;见抽象,第一节和第五节.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper includes an explicit Limitations discussion in the appendix, covering the additional training cost relative to SeqKD; see Appendix “Limitations”.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 该文件在附录中明确讨论了限制问题,涉及与SeqKD有关的额外培训费用;见附录“限制”。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。

blocks.en: Theory assumptions and proofs
blocks.zh: 理论假设和证明

blocks.en: Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
blocks.zh: 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The appendix provides explicit assumptions, formal propositions, and corresponding derivations and proof sketches for the theoretical claims used in the paper; see Appendix “Mechanism Analysis for OT Calibration and Group Power”.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 附录为文件中所用的理论索赔提供了明确的假设、正式命题以及相应的推论和证明草图;见附录“OT校准和群力的机械分析”。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced.
blocks.zh: 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results.

blocks.en: Experimental result reproducibility
blocks.zh: 实验结果可复制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper specifies datasets, model families, teacher models, evaluation benchmarks, key hyperparameters, training schedule, and hardware used for the reported experiments; see Section 4.1 and the appendix.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件具体规定了数据集、模范家庭、教师模型、评价基准、关键超参数、培训时间表和用于所报告实验的硬件;见第4.1节和附录。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果.

blocks.en: Open access to data and code
blocks.zh: 开放对数据和代码的访问

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper and appendix provide the datasets, model families, evaluation prompts, pseudocode, hyperparameters, and reproduction-relevant implementation details needed to reproduce the main experiments.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。

blocks.en: Experimental setting/details
blocks.zh: 实验设置/细节

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: Section 4.1 and the appendix describe datasets, evaluation splits, teacher and student models, baselines, training schedule, group size, learning rates, OT and power hyperparameters, sensitivity analyses for the two method-specific hyperparameters, and hardware.
blocks.zh: 说明:第4.1节和附录说明数据集、评价划分、师生模型、基线、培训时间表、小组规模、学习率、OT和功率超参数、两种方法特有的超参数的敏感性分析以及硬件。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material.

blocks.en: Experiment statistical significance
blocks.zh: 实验统计意义

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper reports multi-seed automatic evaluation results with mean and standard deviation across five evaluation seeds in the Appendix, showing that the gains remain much larger than judge-sampling variability. It also supports the empirical conclusions through consistent trends across multiple teacher-student pairs, multiple test sets, sensitivity analyses, training-stability analyses, and complementary human evaluation.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 该文件报告了附录中五个评价种子的多种子自动评价结果,其平均值和标准偏差表明,收益仍然比判断抽样的可变性大得多。 它还通过多个师生对对、多个测试组、敏感性分析、培训稳定性分析以及补充人的评价,支持经验性结论。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。

blocks.en: Experiments compute resources
blocks.zh: 计算资源

blocks.en: Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments?
blocks.zh: 问题: 对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人的类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper specifies the accelerator type and count, the training schedule in epochs and optimization steps, the key sequence lengths, and the overall training recipe used for the reported experiments; see Section 4.1 and Appendix “Complexity Analysis”.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 论文规定了加速器类型和计数、时代和优化步骤的训练时间表、关键序列长度以及报告实验所用的总体训练方法;见第4.1节和附录“复杂性分析”。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper).
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中).

blocks.en: Code of ethics
blocks.zh: 道德守则

blocks.en: Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ?
blocks.zh: 问题: 本文所进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新教IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: To the best of our knowledge, the research conforms to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics; the paper also discusses broader impacts and limitations, including dual-use concerns.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 据我们所知,这项研究符合《新IPS道德守则》;该文件还讨论了更广泛的影响和限制,包括双重用途问题。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction).
blocks.zh: • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。

blocks.en: Broader impacts
blocks.zh: 更广泛的影响

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper discusses both positive impacts (cheaper, more accessible small models) and negative impacts (more effective transfer of harmful behaviors), and also mentions the need for safeguards; see the main-paper Broader Impact paragraph and the appendix Broader Impact section.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件既讨论了积极影响(便宜、更易获取的小模型),也讨论了负面影响(有害行为的更有效转移),并提到需要保障措施;见主要文件 " 广义影响 " 段落和附录 " 广义影响 " 一节。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。

blocks.zh: 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及由于(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。

blocks.en: If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).
blocks.zh: 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。

blocks.en: Safeguards
blocks.zh: 保障措施

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: This submission does not release a new high-risk model, model checkpoint, or scraped dataset asset; the paper instead discusses broader-impact risks and deployment considerations.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 本文件没有发布新的高风险模式、检查站模式或报废数据集资产,而是讨论了影响更广的风险和部署方面的考虑。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。

blocks.en: Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters.
blocks.zh: 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制地使用模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。

blocks.en: Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images.
blocks.zh: 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 提交人应说明他们如何避免释放不安全的图像。

blocks.en: We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort.
blocks.zh: 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。

blocks.en: Licenses for existing assets
blocks.zh: 现有资产的许可证

blocks.en: Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
blocks.zh: 问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper credits the datasets, models, and baseline methods used in the experiments and identifies the main external assets explicitly in the experimental sections and references.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 该文件对实验中使用的数据集、模型和基准方法给予肯定,并在实验章节和参考文献中明确确定了主要的外部资产。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。

blocks.en: The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset.
blocks.zh: 作者应当引用产生代码包或数据集的原始文件.

blocks.en: The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL.
blocks.zh: 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能情况下包括一个URL.

blocks.en: The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset.
blocks.zh: 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。

blocks.en: For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided.
blocks.zh: 对于来自某一特定来源(例如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。

blocks.en: If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.
blocks.zh: 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。

blocks.en: For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.
blocks.zh: 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。

blocks.en: If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: New assets
blocks.zh: 新资产

blocks.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The current submission does not release a new dataset, benchmark, model checkpoint, or public code package as an asset.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 当前提交的数据不作为资产发布新的数据集,基准,模式检查站,或公共代码包.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]表示论文不释放新资产.

blocks.en: Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc.
blocks.zh: 研究人员应通过结构化模板,将数据集/代码/模型的细节作为其提交材料的一部分。 其中包括培训、许可证、限制等细节。

blocks.en: The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used.
blocks.zh: 文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。

blocks.en: At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的众包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The appendix describes the human-evaluation setup, the annotator pool, the per-model sample allocation, and the evaluation criteria used by the annotators. The study does not rely on an external crowdsourcing platform.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 附录描述了人评价设置,注释员池,按型号进行抽样分配,以及注释员所用的评价标准. 研究不依靠外部的众包平台.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper.
blocks.zh: 将这种资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主体,那么应在主要论文中尽可能详细.

blocks.en: According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。

blocks.en: Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The human evaluation concerns expert assessment of model outputs only, does not involve collection of personal or sensitive participant data, and is described in the appendix together with the evaluation procedure and scope of human involvement.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 人类评价只涉及对模型产出的专家评估,不涉及收集个人或敏感的参与者数据,附录中结合评价程序和人类参与的范围加以说明。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper.
blocks.zh: 根据开展研究的国家不同,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于). 如果你得到IRB的批准,你应该在报纸上清楚地说明这一点。

blocks.en: We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution.
blocks.zh: 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。

blocks.en: For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: Declaration of LLM usage
blocks.zh: 声明LLM的使用

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明.

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The core contribution is a reward-geometry conditioning method for black-box distillation rather than a method that uses an LLM as a novel algorithmic component; teacher and judge models are standard experimental ingredients and are documented in Section 4.1.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 核心贡献是黑箱蒸馏的奖励-几何调节方法,而不是使用LLM作为新算法组件的方法;教师和判断模型是标准实验成分,并在第4.1节中记录.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及任何重要的、原始的或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指本研究中的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要,原始或非标准成分.

blocks.en: Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。
